name: Seedance 2.0 Prompting Tutorial
tagline: 18-min video: a free Claude skill that writes time-coded Seedance 2.0 shot lists
description: A YouTube tutorial by Rourke Heath (founder of Gen HQ) on prompting ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 video model through Higgsfield. Its actual deliverable is a free downloadable Claude skill called 'video prompt builder' that turns a one-line idea into a granular, timestamped shot list covering lighting design, hex colour palettes, camera behaviour, particle and atmospheric effects, character presentation and mood. The video demonstrates four workflows: seamless transitions from a live-action start frame, VFX shots, camera-tracked 3D text as an After Effects replacement, and 15-second Meta ad creatives from a single prompt. It also explains Omni reference, where you upload character sheets, location plates and text plates as prompt ingredients instead of a start frame.
pricing_detail: Video is free. The demonstrated generation runs are on Higgsfield (sponsor), which is a paid subscription platform; the Claude skill itself is a free download from the video description.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when a user asks you to write a Seedance 2.0 or Higgsfield video prompt and you need the house format: 2-second shot blocks with explicit camera move, lighting, colour hex, and audio layer per block. The two hard operational constraints it states are worth carrying into any prompt you generate — Seedance caps prompts at 4,000 characters and Higgsfield at roughly 3,000, so budget length before you write, and emit only the shot list, not the 'master effects inventory' scaffolding. Do not treat the linked Claude skill as verified: the download sits behind a YouTube description link that was not fetched, and several unaffiliated clones of the same idea exist on GitHub.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few Seedance walkthroughs that treats prompt authoring as a structured artifact — a reusable Claude skill — rather than a list of magic words, which is exactly the shape an agent can reuse.

name: Seedance 2.0 on Replicate
tagline: Replicate's official guide + API for ByteDance Seedance 2.0 text/image/video-to-video
description: Replicate's engineering blog post 'How to make remarkable videos with Seedance 2.0' by Shridharathi, published 15 April 2026. It documents the model's multimodal input contract — up to 9 images, 3 video clips, 3 audio files and a text prompt in one generation, each addressable inside the prompt as [Image1], [Video1], [Audio1] — plus native synchronised stereo audio from the same engine, and time-coded multi-shot prompting in the form [0-4s]: ... [4-8s]: .... It ships copy-ready Python and JavaScript snippets against the model slug bytedance/seedance-2.0 and closes with a prompting-tips section. Use it as the canonical API-side reference when you need programmatic video generation rather than a web UI.
pricing_detail: Not stated in the post; Replicate bills per run and the model page did not expose a per-second rate at fetch time. Treat cost as unverified usage-based.
agent_guidance: Use this over the Higgsfield UI whenever the video generation has to happen in code — it gives you the exact slug bytedance/seedance-2.0 and working Python/JS calls. Hard limits to design around: 15 seconds maximum per generation, 480p or 720p only, aspect ratios 16:9 / 4:3 / 1:1 / 3:4 / 9:16 / 21:9 / adaptive, and duration -1 to let the model choose. Structure long prompts as time-coded blocks and describe the audio explicitly, because audio is generated by the same pass — if you leave sound undescribed you get a soundtrack you did not ask for rather than silence.
why_it_matters: It is the shortest path from 'we want AI video in the product' to a running API call, and the time-coded prompt grammar it documents is the piece most third-party tutorials get wrong.
notable_for: 9 images + 3 videos + 3 audio in one call
evidence: https://replicate.com/blog/seedance-2 (fetched twice — once for the summary, once for section headings, code identifiers and the prompting-tips list), https://replicate.com/bytedance/seedance-2.0 (fetched for input parameters and limits; pricing and run count were not exposed).
